text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this huge Premier League fixture as Arsenal host old rivals Manchester United at the Emirates Stadium!
Arsenal have made an unbeaten start to the new campaign, taking seven points from their first three Premier League games, but the Gunners have not been totally convincing.

Mikel Arteta has sought to experiment in a bid to make his side less predictable, but narrow wins over Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace were followed by a dramatic 2-2 draw with Fulham on this ground last week.
A win over United would settle a few nerves in north London and raise hopes of another title push.

Manchester United, meanwhile, have posted two victories and one defeat so far this term, but Erik ten Hag's men were perhaps fortunate to overcome Wolves and Nottingham Forest at home and were truly dreadful in their defeat at Tottenham.
The Red Devils had an abysmal record in away games against the Premier League's finest last season – if they are to build on 2022-23's third-place finish, they simply must improve on their travels.
Arteta makes three changes to the team that started against Fulham, reverting to a tried-and-tested formula.
Thomas Partey has been used at right-back so far this term, but he is out injured.
Gabriel and Zinchenko come into the back four with Kiwior also dropping out, while Nketiah replaces Trossard in attack – he scored twice when these sides last met in January.
Ten Hag is forced into one change to the side that started against Forest last week.
Varane has joined Luke Shaw, Tyrell Malacia and Mason Mount on the injury list, so Lindelof partners Martinez at the back.
The other big piece of news is that new striker Hojlund is fit enough to make the bench.
He's one of four signings among the substitutes, alongside Bayindir, Reguilon and the returning Evans.
United have taken just six points from their last 10 Premier League trips to London clubs (W1 D3 L6), and are winless in their last five in the capital (D2 L3).
Who will edge this battle between two Premier League giants? Kick-off is rapidly approaching, and we're about to find out!
We're under way at the Emirates as Martial gets the ball rolling for United.
There's an electric atmosphere in north London for this one!
Havertz plays a neat ball over the top for Martinelli, but the Brazilian fails to pick out Nketiah or Odegaard with his cross, which Martinez hammers clear.
Martinelli looks up for this game.
He tries to beat Wan-Bissaka on the left before crossing against the United defender to win an early corner for Arsenal.

It's an early test for the United defence as Martinelli receives the ball from a short corner and looks to drive down the byline, with Fernandes opting against a risky challenge before the Arsenal winger sees his cross blocked.

With Manchester City boasting a perfect record and the likes of Tottenham and Liverpool starting the season strongly, both teams will know any missteps could be costly even this early on in the campaign.
There's a real intensity to this match already, just like old times!
Arsenal get some encouragement as United struggle to play through the Gunners' fierce press.
Casemiro then hoists a long pass out of play.
There's a much more familiar look to Arsenal's shape here.
Zinchenko is drifting inside to join Rice in midfield when the Gunners have possession, reprising his role from last season.
Arteta's use of Partey at right-back did not really work in the first few games of the campaign.
United have lost five of their last nine Premier League meetings with Arsenal (W2 D2), one more than they did in their previous 23 against the Gunners in the competition (W12 D7 L4).
United are enjoying plenty of the ball early on, but Arsenal are content to bide their time, choosing their moment to press and attempt to force an error.
United took one point from eight away games against the rest of the Premier League's top nine teams last season.
That record simply has to change if Ten Hag is to enjoy a successful second campaign in the Red Devils' dugout.
Saka embarks on a menacing run down the right before checking back to find Odegaard, who is swiftly crowded out by Casemiro and Eriksen.
United's midfield duo have started well.
GREAT CHANCE FOR ARSENAL! Rice makes a terrific challenge on Fernandes to set the Gunners on the attack.
Martinelli's cross is headed against Martial by Dalot, with the ball then dropping kindly for Havertz.
He has a free shot at goal from eight yards out but completely misses his kick!
Fernandes clears an Arsenal corner from the left, but the hosts retain possession and look to come again.
Wan-Bissaka's sliced clearance only finds Martinelli, who wins another corner.
Onana rises to punch the corner clear, and United get out quickly to stop Saka from having a shot at goal.
The Gunners are coming into this contest after making a slightly cautious start.
We saw one of the best games of the 2022-23 season when these two teams last met in January.
Nketiah – who is back in the Arsenal lineup here and earned an England call-up this week – scored a last-gasp winner as Arsenal triumphed 3-2 on that occasion.
He'd love a repeat of that!
More pressure from Arsenal as Odegaard sees a shot charged down, before Martinelli hangs up a teasing cross towards the far post.
Under pressure from Saka, Dalot nods it behind for a corner.
Over! Saka's corner is met by Rice, but the former West Ham skipper can only send his header over the crossbar.
He should perhaps have done better after losing his man.
United are really struggling to play through the thirds.
Lindelof (24) is the only visiting player to manage more touches so far than Onana's 22.
Arsenal's press is causing issues for the Red Devils.
The home fans are furious as Saka is penalised after challenging Dalot, just as the England international looked to be bearing down on the United penalty area.
Replays show the referee's decision was correct – Dalot was definitely caught.
Now it's Arteta's turn to berate Anthony Taylor as White is left in a heap by Martial's challenge.
The right-back is soon back to his feet, and he will be okay to continue.
Arsenal have lost just two of their last 24 Premier League home games (W18 D4), going down against Manchester City in February and Brighton and Hove Albion in May.
The Gunners have scored in 22 of these 24 games, netting at least twice in 20 of those, but they've also only kept four clean sheets in this run.
Neutrals will be hoping for more goalmouth action here!
Only 10 of United's passes so far have come in the final third.
The Red Devils are being allowed to circulate the ball in their own half, but they're struggling to make any attacking headway.
Antony is very fortunate to avoid a booking, having petulantly kicked the ball away following his foul on Gabriel.
The home fans aren't happy with Taylor here.

GOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAL! RASHFORD SCORES FOR UNITED! The Red Devils score from their first touch in the Arsenal penalty area! Wan-Bissaka almost cedes possession to Martinelli in his own box, but Havertz then plays a sloppy pass straight to Eriksen.
He slides a pass through for Rashford on the break, and the England man cuts inside White before firing a shot off the far post and in.
Eriksen gets the assist, having pounced on a loose pass before finding Rashford's run in behind.
Great vision from the Dane!

GOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAL! ODEGAARD LEVELS IMMEDIATELY! United's lead is wiped out within two minutes! It comes from a flowing Arsenal move as Nketiah picks out Martinelli inside the area, and the Brazilian finds Odegaard with a cutback towards the edge of the box.
Arsenal's captain steadies himself before firing into the bottom-right corner! Arsenal 1-1 Manchester United!
Martinelli has been so lively early on, and he gets the assist for Odegaard's goal after finding his captain in space near the edge of the box!
This game has burst into life now! There was less than two minutes between the two goals, and Arsenal look very up for this now! Saka cuts inside before seeing a teasing cross headed out by Martinez.
Danger for Arsenal! Dalot and Rashford combine on the United left before the latter's cross is taken off Wan-Bissaka's toes by Fernandes.
He tees up Eriksen, who sees a threatening effort deflect just wide!
Arsenal deal with United's corner before looking to break, but a pass towards Nketiah is mishit and the visitors survive.
We've got a real contest on our hands now!
Arsenal have won four of their last five home league games against Manchester United (D1), including the last two in a row.
They last won three in a row against the Red Devils at home between 1988 and 1991.
United's best route to goal certainly seems to be through Rashford on the left flank.
He receives a long ball forward before playing it into Martial, but White and Saliba combine to crowd the striker out.
United have just slowed the pace of the game now, recycling possession in deep areas.
Ten Hag will be furious with his side for letting their lead slip so quickly.
DANGER! Antony loses his footing in the area, allowing Saka to hammer a clearance upfield.
It stays in play as Nketiah looks to beat Lindelof for pace on the Arsenal left, and the United defender scythes the striker down with a desperate challenge.
Lindelof is deservedly booked for that challenge.
Had it taken place in a more central area, the card may have been a different colour.
Over! Rashford steps inside and lets fly from 25 yards out, but his strike is always rising as it whistles beyond the top-right corner.
Saka takes a heavy touch before diving in on Fernandes, catching the United captain on the ankle with his studs.
The winger is booked, and a VAR check decides there is no need to upgrade his card to a red one – there was no intent and the challenge was low to the ground.
Arsenal are enjoying a spell in possession as we enter the closing stages of this opening period.
This game has been played with all the intensity we expect when Arsenal and United face off.
Arsenal threaten as Dalot clears a teasing cross ahead of Saka, before Odegaard gets the Gunners moving again.
He finds Martinelli to his left, and the Brazilian wins a corner with a deflected cross.
United deal with the corner before Antony wins a foul inside his own area, easing the pressure on the visitors.
Fernandes heads Casemiro's long pass against Gabriel before appealing for handball, but there was no chance of a penalty there – the VAR check is swiftly complete.
We're into three additional minutes at the end of this first half, with United back in possession inside their own half.
Martinelli beats Wan-Bissaka again with some fancy footwork before seeing a cross turned behind for a corner.
The United right-back has endured a difficult half.
The corner drops for Nketiah at the far post, and he offloads to Saka.
Saka strides inside before shooting from the edge of the box, but Lindelof makes a crucial block ahead of Onana.
Quick thinking from White, whose throw-in almost sends Nketiah to the byline, only for Martinez to clear behind.
Saka's corner is a deep one, and Havertz turns it comfortably wide.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED.
It's all square as the half-time whistle sounds at the Emirates, with Arsenal and Manchester United locked together at 1-1.
United started cautiously but scored with their first attempt of the game on the counter-attack, with Rashford cutting inside to beat Ramsdale with a fine finish.
Their lead lasted less than two minutes, however, as Odegaard swept home from Martinelli's cutback.
Arsenal have looked threatening since the leveller, with Martinelli their most dangerous player on the left, but it's all to play for in the second half!
United enjoyed 55 per cent of the possession in the opening 45 minutes, but they managed just three shots to Arsenal's nine, and five touches in the area to the Gunners' 16.
However, both teams have managed just one shot on target apiece – both coaches will be demanding more after the interval.
Arsenal get the second half under way! Can the Gunners complete the turnaround to maintain their strong start to the season?
Saliba (31) was the only Arsenal player to better Onana's 30 successful passes in the first half.
That gives an idea of how this game has played out.
Zinchenko wins possession in midfield before sending Saka down the right.
White overlaps to cross, but Onana rises to claim it comfortably.
After 42 minutes, United had played 184 passes in their own half – 49 more than in any other first half they've played in the Premier League this season.
Arsenal have managed to penalty United back, but the visitors have been content to play in deep areas.
Arsenal are enjoying a spell in possession now.
The second half has started at a slow pace, but you get the sense this game could explode into life at any moment.
Odegaard finds Martinelli peeling off at the back post, but Antony gets back to block his compatriot's cross and he even wins a goal-kick.
That was good work from the winger.
Havertz dispossesses Fernandes to get Arsenal on the attack.
The ball is worked right to Odegaard, but his long-range effort is blocked away for a throw-in.
Eriksen looks to scamper away on the counter-attack, but the former Tottenham man stumbles and the ball rolls out for an Arsenal throw.
The home fans enjoyed that.
Wan-Bissaka's loose clearance is picked up by Martinelli, but the United right-back recovers with a strong slide tackle.
Arsenal work the resulting throw into Nketiah, but Lindelof blocks his tame shot from just inside the area.
GREAT OPENING FOR UNITED! Fernandes finds Martial running through on the left side of the box, but Ramsdale makes himself big to turn the Frenchman's powerful drive away.
Rashford follows up with the goal gaping, but Gabriel is on hand to make a massive block.
Saka has been quiet so far for Arsenal.
He has scored on each of his last three Premier League appearances against Manchester United – no player in Arsenal's history has ever scored in four consecutive league games against the Red Devils.
Arsenal win a left-wing corner and work it short to Nketiah.
He fails to find space for a shot but Arsenal keep the attack alive, and Fernandes eventually fouls Martinelli near the corner flag.
Martinelli delivers the free-kick low towards the near post, where it is flicked on and eventually hacked clear by Lindelof.
PENALTY TO ARSENAL! Havertz receives a pass from Nketiah before darting between Wan-Bissaka and Casemiro into the box.
He's set to pull the trigger, but Wan-Bissaka dangles a foot and brings him down.
Anthony Taylor wastes no time in pointing to the spot, but there's a VAR check to confirm it...
Well, well.
The referee has been sent to the monitor to review the incident! The contact was only slight, so Wan-Bissaka may receive a huge reprieve!
NO PENALTY! The referee scrutinises the collision at the VAR monitor, and while there was contact between Wan-Bissaka's hip and Havertz, it isn't deemed sufficient to send the German over.
Anthony Taylor signals that the penalty will not stand!
Odegaard works space for a shot on the left side of the penalty area, but he lifts a tame attempt straight at Onana.
United break quickly, but Saliba matches Rashford stride-for-stride to force them back.
Martinelli stands a cross up for Saka, but Dalot watches it carefully before making a crucial defensive header.
United look set to introduce new striker Hojlund for his debut shortly...
Martinez is booked for a clumsy foul on Nketiah.
The referee played advantage, with Martinelli eventually seeing a cross headed behind for an Arsenal corner.
Martinez goes down before Arsenal can take their corner.
The Argentine hurt himself while fouling Nketiah, and forgotten man Harry Maguire looks likely to replace him from the bench! It's another defensive injury for Ten Hag to deal with.
Hojlund makes his Manchester United debut after joining from Atalanta! He replaces Martial.
Maguire is also on in advance of the Arsenal corner, with Martinez unable to continue.
SO CLOSE TO 2-1! Arsenal pull the corner back to Martinelli, who side-foots just wide from 20 yards out! Onana wasn't getting to that one, and he was grateful to see it roll wide of the post!
Onana is booked for timewasting ahead of United's goal-kick.
He then punts the ball downfield in a change of approach from the visitors.
Hojlund battles with Gabriel to reach a long ball forward, but the new recruit comes out second-best as the Arsenal defender holds his own.
United have been in need of a focal point – can Hojlund make an immediate impact?
Rashford's opener made him just the second United player to score in three consecutive Premier League appearances against Arsenal, after former Gunner Robin van Persie did so between 2012 and 2013.
He has been quiet since the break, however.
Arsenal are living dangerously as Rashford beats White and advances down the byline.
He tries to find Hojlund with his cutback, but Saliba is there to smother the attempt, allowing the hosts to clear.
Rice plays a neat one-two with Havertz but Antony is on hand to intercept the midfielder's next pass.
Arsenal have lost their way in attack since seeing their penalty award overturned by the VAR earlier in this half.
Fernandes finds Rashford in a dangerous position on the United left, and the England international wins a corner off Saliba.
The set-piece is worked out to Antony on the edge, but his tame effort is blocked.
Both teams need more composure in the final third.
Arteta is preparing three changes as Arsenal hunt a winner, with Jesus among the players waiting to enter the action.
Jesus replaces Nketiah.
There will be no repeat of January's late heroics against United for him.
Tomiyasu, meanwhile, comes on for Zinchenko.
Vieira replaces Havertz, who has been quiet, in Arsenal's third substitution.
Saka looks to reach a return pass from Odegaard before going down under pressure from Dalot.
There was nothing doing there, it was another strong intervention from United's stand-in left-back.
United waste a good opening on the break! Rashford has support from Hojlund but opts to cut inside and shoot from the left, and he can only send his effort into a crowd of red shirts.
We're into the final 10 minutes of the 90 and this contest remains finely poised.
Can either team find a winner?
HUGE CHANCE FOR SAKA! Arsenal should be 2-1 up! Martinelli glides infield with more excellent footwork before finding Odegaard, who pauses before offloading to White on the right side of the box.
His low cross drops perfectly for Saka eight yards out, but he side-foots straight at Onana! That was the best opportunity of the second half!
Onana knew very little about that last save – if Saka had placed his shot anywhere else in the goal, the Gunners would be 2-1 up! Will they get another chance to win it?
Garnacho replaces Antony as Ten Hag refreshes his attack.
The Brazilian has put a good shift in here.
Evans gets a second United debut, with Lindelof withdrawn.
That must be due to another fitness concern, and United now have a makeshift partnership of Evans and Maguire!
Wan-Bissaka concedes a corner, but Martinelli's terrible delivery is hacked clear at the near post.
Arsenal have to do much better than that.
Is this the moment for Hojlund? No! The striker races onto a pass from Casemiro before cutting inside Gabriel, but the defender stands firm to make a clean challenge inside his own area.
That was another promising counter-attack from United.

GOAAAAAAAAAAAL! GARNACHO SURELY WINS IT FOR UNITED! The Emirates is stunned as Garnacho races onto Casemiro's throughball before slotting beyond Ramsdale and into the bottom-right corner! The travelling fans go wild behind that goal, but there will be a VAR check! Garnacho may have strayed beyond the last defender!

THE VAR REVIEW IS OVER, THE GOAL IS OVERTURNED! Garnacho is disconsolate as the VAR review rules he was marginally ahead of Gabriel when racing onto that pass! It remains 1-1 here, and the home crowd have been whipped into a frenzy by that let-off!
Gabriel is booked for dissent, but the decision has gone his way.
Garnacho was narrowly offside!
Nelson replaces Martinelli on the Arsenal left as we enter EIGHT minutes of stoppage time.
Can either team find a decisive goal?
That's one VAR reprieve apiece in the second half.
Havertz was denied a penalty at one end, with Garnacho denied a potential winning goal at the other.
It's all Arsenal now as Nelson darts down the left wing before crossing towards Saka, but Evans gets there to make a crucial interception.
Possession is quickly back with the Gunners, however – is there one more twist to come?
Jesus twists and turns before finding Odegaard just outside the box, and his powerful shot deflects over! Arsenal have a late chance from this corner...
GOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLL! RICE WINS IT FOR ARSENAL! This is remarkable! Saka's deep delivery drops to Rice at the far post, with the midfielder able to chest it down before volleying at goal.
His strike takes a slight deflection off Evans before beating Onana at his near post! Arsenal lead 2-1 at the death!
Saka gets the assist, with his deep delivery landing right on Rice's chest.
There was a hint of fortune about Rice's finish, but the Arsenal fans don't care!
Jorginho replaces Odegaard as Arteta looks to run down the clock.
Surely the Gunners have done enough?
United go direct from the kick-off, but the ball is with Ramsdale! Ten Hag looks crestfallen on the sidelines – it's more late heartbreak for United on this ground!
United try to forge one last chance as Dalot hurls a long throw into Arsenal's area.
Hojlund tries to bring it down... but Nelson clears! United will come again...
GOAAAAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLL! JESUS FINISHES UNITED OFF ON THE BREAK! United lift a deep free-kick into the area, but Arsenal scramble it clear.

Vieira then finds Jesus darting through on the break, and the Brazilian keeps his composure to sit Dalot down before slotting past Onana! Arsenal 3-1 Manchester United, and that will be that at the Emirates!
Vieira gets the assist by sending Jesus clean through on goal as United threw men forward in search of a leveller.
The substitute did the rest with a composed finish!
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 3-1 MANCHESTER UNITED.

The full-time whistle sounds at a jubilant Emirates Stadium, and two stoppage-time goals give Arsenal a huge 3-1 win over Manchester United! The game looked to be petering out towards a draw after two VAR reviews saw Havertz denied a penalty at one end, and Garnacho denied a potential winner at the other.
Arsenal, however, had other ideas.
Rice's deflected strike beat Onana to provoke wild celebrations from the home fans, before Jesus rounded off the scoring on the break! What a win for the Gunners!
Arsenal join Tottenham, Liverpool and West Ham on 10 points after four games of the Premier League season.
What a way for the Gunners to sign off for the international break, after which they go to Everton.
United, meanwhile, find themselves in the bottom half with two wins and two defeats – they will have to pick themselves up to face Brighton on September 16.
We hope you have enjoyed our coverage of a dramatic victory for Arsenal.
It's goodbye from us, and we'll see you next time.
